transcription.notes: A different cipher from the other three: the Feria-Mansfeld key, transcribed to keyM.tsv.

system.summary: Spanish office cipher of 1592-93: two-digit numbers carry consonant-vowel syllables, a small homophonic symbol alphabet carries bare letters, diacritics add a final consonant, and two- and three-letter groups carry the nomenclature; no. 68 is a second cipher of the same office (Feria-Mansfeld, 1593) with three-letter word codes and higher figures.

diacritics.note: Dot above = final -l, + = -m, dot after = -n, : = -r, ^ = -s, ring = -h-; bar above = the number itself; umlaut = doubled consonant; a top sign marks a code word. Confirmed on plaintext (achaque, bolsa, del passado, con).

system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's key images phelippes2.png (Spanish Cipher 1592-1593) and spanish3mansfeld.png (Feria/Mansfeld 1593), published on cryptiana as images; and the office's own key, BnF fr. 3995 fol. 97 (canvas 188), found through DECODE key records 4076 and 4077
system.notes: fr. 3995 f. 97 confirms Tomokiyo's syllable table against the original and adds the nomenclature he lacks (aunque, alli, armas, autoridad, causa, exercito, estados, election, Francia, magestad, ministro, negocios, Rey, Reyno, religion, reputacion, Roma, seignor and more). fr. 3995 f. 101 was checked and excluded: it is an Italian nomenclature belonging to another correspondence.

prior_solution.where: Keys published by Tomokiyo as images on cryptiana (spanish3.htm), reconstructed from other letters with no published reading of these four; the office's own key survives at BnF fr. 3995 f. 97 and is catalogued on DECODE as records 4076-4077; a contemporary decipherer glossed part of no. 47. No published reading of any of the four letters.

conditions.human_role: Project-level only: the target was taken from the repository's catalogue and worked by the model in Claude Code; no target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Tomokiyo's Spanish page fetched as HTML rather than as the text dump in gallica_sweep/src: his key tables are images, and two of them cover exactly the folios this entry cites.

The catalogue's piece numbers resolved to folios through the BnF depouillement, and the folio-to-canvas map for fr. 3983 and fr. 3984 built by reading folio numbers off top strips and interpolating; all four leaves located.

Tomokiyo's Spanish Cipher (1592-93) transcribed to key92.tsv and applied to nos. 45 and 79: Spanish comes out (supongo que hava de ser, siendo confidente, a costa de la bolsa, a los sucesores, conviene), but with holes wherever the nomenclator is used.
No. 68's figures run far higher and the leaf carries three-letter word groups, so it is the Feria-Mansfeld cipher, as Tomokiyo's citation of f. 145 says, not the cipher of the other three.

The entry's own verify step followed: DECODE returns two records for these correspondents and both are keys, not letters, pointing into BnF fr. 3995. Folio 97 is the office's own key, complete with the nomenclature Tomokiyo lacks; key92.tsv extended to 133 entries.

The contemporary interlinear gloss on no. 47 checked against the key's own output on a third letter: del Passado con, por via de mar, difiriendo de dia en dia - agreement wherever both survive, and the bar, umlaut and trailing dot settled.
All four leaves read line by line from deskewed strips: 15 of 17 lines on no. 45, 14 of 16 on no. 79, the glossed lines on no. 47, and the opening of no. 68 with keyM.tsv.
The obvious candidate for the missing Feria-Mansfeld nomenclature, fr. 3995 f. 101, fetched and excluded: it is an Italian nomenclature belonging to another correspondence.

Novelty re-examined. G. Lasry (21 Sept 2026): on cryptiana 'undeciphered' means no interlinear or nearby deciphered copy, not unsolved; unsolved material is on the unsolved page. 'Never applied' replaced by 'no published reading'.

outcome.method_basis: Tomokiyo's cryptiana key images (Spanish Cipher 1592-93 and the Feria-Mansfeld cipher) cite these very folios (fr. 3983 ff. 98, 162; fr. 3984 f. 145), and the office's own key at BnF fr. 3995 f. 97 (DECODE R4076-R4077, returned by a search for these correspondents) supplied the nomenclator; the interlinear gloss on no. 47 checked it.
outcome.fraction_read_source: reading45/79/47/68.md tables: 935 cipher tokens in transcribed rows, 124 unresolved '·' groups; untranscribed lines added at mean line length (~114 tokens: no.45 1 line, no.79 2, no.47 lines 6, 8 and later); no.68 lines 7-10 (~90 tokens that decode to syllables but not Spanish, Feria-Mansfeld nomenclature missing) counted unread; ~720/1050. Dots undercount multi-group gaps, so this is an upper bound
outcome.notes: Three letters read in substance on the office key and checked against a contemporary decipherment; a scatter of groups in every letter and the later lines remain, and the nomenclature of the Feria-Mansfeld cipher of no. 68 is the one real gap. fraction_read measured from the four reading tables (see fraction_read_source). Key partial: 1592-93 office key complete (fr. 3995 f. 97) but the Feria-Mansfeld nomenclature is missing; codes_open.open counts only the ten Mansfeld groups named in NOTES, not the scatter of '·' groups.
